take_homes: Access is not uptake: everyone could read every folder, but what people actually picked up from each other is the smaller number. I'll use that before anyone promises a percentage.
The real bottleneck is whether my organisation writes down what it knows and others pick it up, faster than the models change. That is a learning and people question.
Ask 'what would have to show up for us to drop this?' of any plan, and a person decides which assumptions to test.

monday.move: Draft an agent that prepares my weekly people-metrics summary, with no employee-level data at first, and show it to one HR partner. Also bring the 'access is not uptake' question to the leadership team.
monday.who: Me and one HR business partner
monday.when: Thursday, after I have talked to my DPO
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO or works council says employee data can't go into the tool, I stop and use only aggregated or invented data.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I haven't asked yet.

misconception.why: Nothing here said which roles go. But 'who writes it down and who picks it up' made me think the first question is whether we learn fast enough, not which headcount goes. I'm not convinced yet.

one_line: The room exercise was long and heavy on jargon, but the one idea worth my time was that access isn't uptake, and the module never says what this means for the people doing the work.
